verses.1:1: The word of the Lord that came to Joel the son of Bethuel.
verses.1:2: Hear these things, elders, and listen closely, all who inhabit the land. Have such things happened in our days, or in the days of your fathers?
verses.1:3: Give an account of them to your children, and your children to their children, and their children to another generation.
verses.1:4: What the caterpillar left, the locust devoured; and what the locust left, the wingless locust devoured; and what the wingless locust left, the blight devoured.
verses.1:5: Sober up, drunkards, from their wine, and weep; lament, all who drink wine, to drunkenness, because gladness and joy have been taken away from your mouth.
verses.1:6: For a nation has come up against My land, strong and innumerable; its teeth are the teeth of a lion, and its molars are those of a young lion.
verses.1:7: It has reduced My vine to desolation, and My fig trees to splinters; it has thoroughly searched it out and thrown it away; it has whitened its branches.
verses.1:8: Lament to Me more than a bride girded with sackcloth over the husband of her virginity.
verses.1:9: Sacrifice and drink offering have been taken away from the house of the Lord; mourn, priests who minister at the altar.
verses.1:10: Because the plains are devastated, let the land mourn; because grain is devastated, wine has dried up, oil has diminished,
verses.1:11: farmers have dried up. Lament, estates, over wheat and barley, because the harvest has perished from the field;
verses.1:12: the vine has dried up, and the fig trees have diminished; pomegranate and palm and apple and all the trees of the field have dried up, because the sons of men have put joy to shame.
verses.1:13: Gird yourselves and wail, priests; lament, you who minister at the altar. Come in, sleep in sackcloth, you who minister to God, because sacrifice and drink offering have been kept back from the house of your God.
verses.1:14: Sanctify a fast, proclaim a service, gather elders, all who inhabit the land, into the house of your God, and cry out to the Lord earnestly:
verses.1:15: "Alas, alas, alas for the day, for the day of the Lord is near, and like devastation from devastation it will come."
verses.1:16: Before your eyes food has been utterly destroyed; from the house of your God, gladness and joy.
verses.1:17: Heifers have leaped at their mangers, storehouses have been laid waste, vats have been torn down, because grain has dried up.
verses.1:18: What will we store up for ourselves? Herds of cattle have wept, because there was no pasture for them, and the flocks of sheep have been wiped out.
verses.1:19: To You, Lord, I will cry out, because fire has consumed the lovely places of the wilderness, and a flame has set ablaze all the trees of the field;
verses.1:20: and the beasts of the plain have looked up to You, because channels of water have dried up, and fire has devoured the lovely places of the wilderness.
verses.2:1: Sound a trumpet in Zion, proclaim on My holy mountain, and let all who inhabit the land be thrown into confusion, because the day of the Lord is here, for it is near:
verses.2:2: a day of darkness and gloom, a day of cloud and mist. Like dawn a numerous and strong people will be poured out upon the mountains; one like it has not been from ages past, and after it none will be added, even to years for generations of generations.
verses.2:3: In front of it is a consuming fire, and behind it a blazing flame; like a garden of delight is the land before its face, and behind it a plain of desolation, and there will be no one who escapes it.
verses.2:4: Like the appearance of horses is their appearance, and like horsemen, so they will pursue;
verses.2:5: like the sound of chariots they will leap upon the tops of the mountains, and like the sound of a flame of fire devouring stubble, and like a numerous and strong people arrayed for war.
verses.2:6: Before its face peoples will be crushed, every face like the scorch of a pot.
verses.2:7: Like warriors they will run, and like men of war they will climb upon the walls; and each one will march in his own way, and they will by no means turn aside from their paths,
verses.2:8: and each one will not keep away from his brother; weighed down in their armor they will march, and among their missiles they will fall, and they will by no means be brought to an end.
verses.2:9: They will seize the city, and upon the walls they will run, and upon the houses they will climb, and through windows they will enter like thieves.
verses.2:10: Before its face the earth will be thrown into confusion and heaven will be shaken; the sun and the moon will grow dark, and the stars will dim their brightness.
verses.2:11: And the Lord will utter His voice before His force, because His camp is exceedingly numerous, because strong are the works of His words; for great is the day of the Lord, great and exceedingly manifest, and who will be equal to it?
verses.2:12: And now the Lord your God says, "Turn back to Me with all your heart, and with fasting and with weeping and with wailing,
verses.2:13: and tear your hearts and not your garments, and turn back to the Lord your God, because He is merciful and compassionate, patient and rich in mercy, and relenting over the calamities."
verses.2:14: Who knows whether He will turn back and relent, and leave behind Him a blessing, a sacrifice and a drink offering for the Lord our God?
verses.2:15: Sound a trumpet in Zion, sanctify a fast, proclaim a service,
verses.2:16: gather the people, sanctify an assembly, choose elders, gather infants nursing at the breasts; let a bridegroom come out from his bedroom and a bride from her bridal chamber.
verses.2:17: In the midst of the platform of the altar the priests who minister to the Lord will weep and say, "Spare Your people, Lord, and do not give Your inheritance to reproach, for nations to rule over them, so that they may not say among the nations, 'Where is their God?'"
verses.2:18: And the Lord became zealous for His land, and spared His people.
verses.2:19: And the Lord answered and said to His people, "Look, I am sending you the grain and the wine and the oil, and you will be filled with them, and I will no longer give you to reproach among the nations;
verses.2:20: and the one from the north I will drive away from you, and I will drive him out into a waterless land, and I will make his front vanish into the first sea, and his rear into the last sea; and his rottenness will rise up, and his stench will rise up, because he has magnified his works."
verses.2:21: Take courage, land, rejoice and be glad, because the Lord has acted greatly.
verses.2:22: Take courage, beasts of the plain, because the plains of the wilderness have sprouted, because the tree has borne its fruit; fig tree and vine have given their strength.
verses.2:23: And children of Zion, rejoice and be glad in the Lord your God, because He has given you food for righteousness, and He will rain down for you early and late rain, as before,
verses.2:24: and the threshing floors will be filled with grain, and the vats will overflow with wine and oil.
verses.2:25: And He will repay you for the years that the locust and the wingless locust and the blight and the caterpillar devoured, My great force that I sent against you;
verses.2:26: and you will eat and eat and be filled, and you will praise the name of the Lord your God for the things He has done with you as marvels, and My people will by no means be put to shame forever;
verses.2:27: and you will recognize that I am in the midst of Israel, and that I am the Lord your God, and there is no other besides Me, and My people will by no means be put to shame again, forever.
verses.3:1: And it will be after these things that I will pour out from My Spirit upon all flesh, and your sons and your daughters will prophesy, and your old men will dream dreams, and your young men will see visions;
verses.3:2: and even upon My male slaves and upon the female slaves in those days I will pour out from My Spirit;
verses.3:3: and I will give wonders in heaven, and upon the earth blood and fire and vapor of smoke;
verses.3:4: the sun will be turned into darkness and the moon into blood before the great and manifest day of the Lord comes;
verses.3:5: and it will be that everyone who calls upon the name of the Lord will be saved; for on Mount Zion and in Jerusalem there will be one who escapes, just as the Lord said, and those to whom good news is proclaimed, whom the Lord has summoned.
verses.4:1: For look, I, in those days and at that time, when I restore the captivity of Judah and Jerusalem,
verses.4:2: will gather all the nations and bring them down into the valley of Jehoshaphat, and I will enter into judgment with them there on behalf of My people and My inheritance Israel, who were scattered among the nations; and they divided up My land,
verses.4:3: and they cast lots for My people, and they gave the boys to prostitutes, and they sold the girls for wine and drank.
verses.4:4: And what are you to Me, Tyre and Sidon, and all Galilee of the foreigners? Are you paying back a repayment to Me? Or are you sharply holding a grudge against Me? And swiftly I will pay back your repayment onto your heads,
verses.4:5: because you took My silver and My gold, and you brought My choice and fine things into your temples;
verses.4:6: and you sold the sons of Judah and the sons of Jerusalem to the sons of the Greeks, so that you might drive them out from their borders.
verses.4:7: Look, I am rousing them from the place where you sold them, and I will pay back your repayment onto your heads,
verses.4:8: and I will sell your sons and your daughters into the hands of the sons of Judah, and they will sell them into captivity to a nation far away, for the Lord has spoken.
verses.4:9: Proclaim these things among the nations: consecrate war, rouse the warriors, and draw near and come up, all you men of war;
verses.4:10: beat your plows into swords and your sickles into spears; let the weak one say, "I am strong."
verses.4:11: Assemble and come in, all you nations all around, and be gathered there; let the meek one be a warrior.
verses.4:12: Let them be roused, let all the nations come up into the valley of Jehoshaphat, for there I will sit to judge all the nations all around.
verses.4:13: Send out sickles, for the grape harvest is at hand; come in, tread, because the winepress is full; make the vats overflow, for their evils have multiplied.
verses.4:14: Sounds resounded in the valley of judgment, for the day of the Lord is near in the valley of judgment.
verses.4:15: The sun and the moon will grow dark, and the stars will withdraw their radiance.
verses.4:16: And the Lord will cry out from Zion, and from Jerusalem He will utter His voice, and heaven and earth will be shaken; but the Lord will spare His people and will strengthen the sons of Israel.
verses.4:17: And you will know that I am the Lord your God, dwelling in Zion, on My holy mountain; and Jerusalem will be holy, and foreigners will no longer pass through her.
verses.4:18: And it will be in that day that the mountains will drip sweetness, and the hills will flow with milk, and all the channels of Judah will flow with waters, and a spring will come out from the house of the Lord and will water the wadi of the rushes.
verses.4:19: Egypt will become a desolation, and Idumea will become a plain of desolation because of the injustices against the sons of Judah, because they shed righteous blood in their land.
verses.4:20: But Judea will be inhabited forever, and Jerusalem for generations of generations;
verses.4:21: and I will avenge their blood and will by no means acquit, and the Lord will dwell in Zion.

notes.1:1: The Greek reads Bathouel (standard English "Bethuel"), differing from the Hebrew Masoretic Text's "Pethuel."
notes.1:4: The Greek identifies the four scourges as caterpillar (kampe), locust (akris), wingless locust (brouchos), and blight (erysibe), rendering four Hebrew terms for locusts.
notes.1:15: The Greek renders the Hebrew wordplay "destruction from Shaddai (the Almighty)" as "devastation from devastation" (talaiporia ek talaiporias), and repeats the lament exclamation "Alas" (oimoi) three times.
notes.1:17: The Greek reads "Heifers have leaped at their mangers," a striking divergence from the Hebrew Masoretic Text's "The seeds shriveled under their clods."
notes.1:18: The Greek opens with the question "What will we store up for ourselves?" where the Hebrew Masoretic Text has "How the beasts groan!"
notes.2:6: The Greek phrase "the scorch of a pot" (proskauma chytras) describes faces blackened with dread, interpreting a difficult Hebrew expression.
notes.2:17: The Greek reads "in the midst of the platform [krepis] of the altar" with no conjunction before "altar," whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text has "between the vestibule and the altar."
notes.2:20: The "first sea" and "last sea" reflect the Greek rendering of the eastern (Dead) and western (Mediterranean) seas; the spelling bromos here serves as an orthographic variant of bromos ("stench").
notes.2:23: The Greek renders the Hebrew phrase for the autumn rain (or teacher) as "food" (ta bromata), yielding "food for righteousness."
notes.2:25: The Greek shifts within the verse from third person ("He will repay," antapodosei) to first person ("My great force that I sent"), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text uses first person throughout.
notes.3:2: The Greek includes "My" with "male slaves" (tous doulous mou) but not with "female slaves" (tas doulas); the Hebrew Masoretic Text omits "My" on both, whereas Acts 2:18 includes it on both.
notes.3:3: The Greek renders the Hebrew "columns of smoke" as "vapor of smoke" (atmida kapnou).
notes.3:5: The Greek reads euangelizomenoi ("those to whom good news is proclaimed," or in the middle voice "those proclaiming good news"), where the Hebrew Masoretic Text has "among the survivors."
notes.4:4: The Greek uses the proper name "Galilee of the foreigners" where the Hebrew reads "regions of Philistia" (the Septuagint regularly renders Philistines as "foreigners"), and punctuates "sharply" with the preceding question before "And swiftly."
notes.4:8: The Greek reads "into captivity" rather than the Hebrew "to the Sabeans," reflecting a different vocalization of the Hebrew consonants.
notes.4:11: The Greek reads "let the meek one be a warrior," diverging from the Hebrew text ("bring down your mighty ones").
notes.4:14: The Greek reads "Sounds resounded in the valley of judgment," translating the Hebrew "Multitudes, multitudes in the valley of decision" through the verbal sense of clamor/roaring and a courtroom rendering of the valley's name.
notes.4:19: The Greek uses the Hellenistic territorial name "Idumea" for Edom (paralleling "Judea" in 4:20) and renders "desolate wilderness" as "plain of desolation."
